classification.difficultyReason: Construct a triangle from three sides and explain impossible side-length combinations using the triangle inequality; SSS is the closest available catalogue skill.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Using a ruler and compasses only, construct a triangle with side lengths of 6 cm, 8 cm and 5 cm.

answer.short: A triangle with sides 6 cm, 8 cm and 5 cm, constructed using intersecting compass arcs.
answer.worked: Draw $AB=8$ cm. Draw an arc with centre $A$ and radius 6 cm, then an arc with centre $B$ and radius 5 cm. Label an intersection $C$. Join $AC$ and $BC$, retaining the construction arcs. Either reflected position of $C$ is valid.

spec.description: Authored solution construction with an 8 cm baseline and intersecting arcs of radii 6 cm and 5 cm. No diagram is supplied in the student source.
spec.mathematics: AB=8 cm, AC=6 cm and BC=5 cm; C is an intersection of the two compass arcs.

children.label: i
children.prompt: What happens when you try to construct a triangle with side lengths of 4 cm, 5 cm and 12 cm?

answer.short: It is impossible: $4+5=9<12$, so the compass circles do not intersect.
answer.worked: Draw a 12 cm baseline. Circles centred at its endpoints with radii 4 cm and 5 cm do not meet, because $4+5=9<12$. There is no third vertex, so the triangle cannot be constructed.

inlines.text: Copy and complete: ‘The longest side of a triangle …’
The longest side of a triangle

inlines.answer: is shorter than the sum of the other two sides.

answer.short: The longest side of a triangle is shorter than the sum of the other two sides.
answer.worked: The longest side must be shorter than the sum of the other two sides. This is the triangle inequality; otherwise the two shorter sides cannot meet to form a triangle.

children.label: c
children.prompt: Jack says that in the Great Outback there are three towns $A$, $B$ and $C$. Town $B$ is 34 km from $A$ and 68 km from $C$. Town $A$ is 110 km from $C$. (All distances are as the crow flies.) Comment on Jack’s claim.

answer.short: Jack’s claim is false: $34+68=102<110$, contradicting the triangle inequality.
answer.worked:
$$AB+BC=34+68=102\text{ km}$$
The direct distance $AC$ cannot exceed the distance from $A$ to $C$ via $B$. Since $110>102$, the stated distances are impossible, so Jack’s claim is false.
